Definition: from G2596 and G138 (including its alternate); to lower (or with violence) demolish (literally or figuratively):--cast (pull, put, take) down, destroy.
BiblicalUsage: To pull down is to lower with force, and Mary sang that God has put down the mighty from their seats and exalted them of low degree, and God destroyed seven nations and gave their land to Israel, and Paul says the weapons of our warfare are mighty to the pulling down of strong holds, and Joseph took the body of Jesus down from the cross. The word holds the throne, the nation, the stronghold, and the cross together, and God pulls down what stands against Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God pulls down the mighty and lifts up the lowly, and the cross is where both happened at once. I hold that my weapons are not carnal but mighty through God, and the strongholds in my own heart are the first ones to fall.
